investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-16T12:25–12:33Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained unscheduled for 127–144 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the runner could not collect any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable slots and no preemption candidates, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract misconfiguration. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this scheduling blockage: the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885, createAgent call) never receives a running VM, so it cannot populate vmIdPresent or remoteState, and the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256 is violated in full.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node label drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes also lose capacity, the effective pool is zero. This could be a pre-existing constraint or a recent node label change not reflected in the evidence.
Tertiary — resource quota or limit range at the namespace level preventing additional kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations beyond the current count, compounding the per-node exhaustion.

Lower confidence — a transient spike in concurrent remote-agent creation requests (e.g., from other users or automated jobs) consuming all VM slots simultaneously with the eval run, causing a temporary but not permanent capacity shortage.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod provisioned by the eval runner was stuck unschedulable: the Kubernetes cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, no agent was ever created, and the remote-agent-state check produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource exhausted or quota reached), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. As a result, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) never returned a live agent, the probe timed out after ~143–150 s, and no evidence payload was written — causing the contract validation to fail on all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote agent VM provisioning layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained unscheduled for 127–144 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the runner could not collect any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector.
